judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insuring clause is a short promise to pay proceeds 'according to the following provisions'; the text as reproduced is garbled but the operative promise is conventional and does not name any indeterminate term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply subordinates itself to Sections 3-10 (e.g. 4.1 Payment of Proceeds), so it harmonises rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard 20-day free-look with a refund of 'any premium you have paid'; the wording is corrupted in transcription but the mechanism (return within 20 days, void from the beginning) is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with 3.1 (premium payable at or before delivery) and 7.2 (effective date); no competing provision addresses rescission.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paid-up benefit is stated only in fragments — 'level amount based on: a. The current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness' — so the actual amount of paid-up insurance and the triggering birthday are left indeterminate on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with 4.2 (death benefit tied to Specified Amount and Coverage Option) and with the Maturity Date in Section 1, and the relationship between an automatic paid-up conversion and continuing Monthly Insurance Charges under 5.3/5.10 is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory statement that definitions are subordinate to the fuller description in Sections 3-10; 'more complete description' is loose but nothing operative turns on it alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It functions as an internal priority rule, so where a Section 2 definition diverges from an operative section (e.g. 2.15 vs 5.3) this clause is what a court would use to harmonise them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition identifying the Insured as the person listed in Section 1 whose death causes proceeds to be paid; the transcription is broken but the concept is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2 (Owner may be someone other than the Insured) and 4.1; no tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You or Your' means the Owner, expressly allowing the Owner to differ from the Insured; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 8.1-8.3 ownership provisions and Section 1's designation of the same person as Owner and Insured; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We or Us' identifies the insurer; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout Sections 3-10; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition breaks off after 'as named in the original [application] but may subsequently be changed as provided', so as reproduced it does not complete the change mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 8.4, which adds that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named and deals with predeceasing beneficiaries; the definition alone is incomplete rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceeds' is defined as the total amount payable on death or on surrender, a definite two-branch definition cross-referencing Section 4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.1 pays 'Surrender Value' on surrender and 'Death Proceeds' on death, and 9.4 deducts indebtedness from 'Policy Proceeds'; the several proceeds labels are close but not obviously inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Policy Date is the computation anchor shown in Section 1; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.17 (Monthly Due Date same day as Policy Date) and 7.2 (effect on later of Policy Date or premium payment).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The date coverage commences' is a short definition that defers to Section 7.2, 6.2 and riders; the reference to '% 2' is a transcription artefact rather than a naming of a genuinely ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.1 says there is no coverage until premium is paid while 7.2 sets effect on the later of Policy Date or payment; the definition points to 7.2 and largely harmonises, but the interplay with the Temporary Insurance Agreement is left open.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment survives — 'upon the Insured's age on the birthday nearest the first' — so the age convention (age nearest birthday as of what date) cannot be applied from the clause itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Age drives the 5.4 Cost of Insurance table and the 4.2 risk-percentage corridor, so an incomplete age definition has real downstream consequences, though no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says premium amount and frequency are what the Owner 'most recently elect[s]' yet also that during the first two Policy years the Section 1 figure 'is the minimum that must be paid' — a flexible-premium description carrying a mandatory floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with 3.2(1)-(2) (same two-year minimum expressed differently) and with 5.10's no-lapse guarantee keyed to one-twelfth of the Planned Periodic Premium; the three formulations are similar but not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition requiring the Minimum Initial Premium before delivery, with the amount left to Section 1; definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.1 says it must be paid 'at or before' delivery and 7.2 makes the effective date turn on payment; 'before' versus 'at or before' is a slight but real divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated mid-sentence, leaving 'the amount you specified in the original application' and the increase/decrease right without their qualifying words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2 supplies the change conditions and 5.9 reduces the Specified Amount on withdrawal under Option A; the definition defers to those and does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Death Benefit is defined as the amount payable 'prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4', depending on Specified Amount and Coverage Option; the deferral is clear even though the text is corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with 4.2's greater-of formulas and with 4.2's later adjustments for riders and indebtedness; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Both coverage options provide for an increased death benefit when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' uses the undefined and vague phrase 'a minimum size'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The corridor is actually implemented by the risk-percentage table in 4.2, so the definition's loose phrase is filled in there; the fit is workable but the definition overstates its own generality.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of Monthly Insurance Charge is itself clear (Cost of Insurance plus rider costs deducted on each Monthly Due Date).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs the reader to 'Section 4.3', but the Monthly Insurance Charge provision is 5.3 (4.3 is Interest on Death Proceeds), a mis-cross-reference of the kind courts must correct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cost of Insurance is the charge for 'pure insurance protection' at current rates, expressly excluding rider costs; the phrase is standard and cross-referenced to 5.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.3 (charge equals COI plus rider costs) and 5.5; no divergence found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Monthly Due Date is fixed as the same day of each month as the Policy Date; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in 4.2, 5.1, 5.3 and 5.10; no inconsistency, though 5.4 refers instead to a 'Premium Due Date'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'There is no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' is categorical, and the alternative 'Planned Periodic Premium or Minimum Initial Premium' leaves which one must be paid to the insurer's or owner's choice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 makes coverage effective on the later of the Policy Date or payment and preserves a Temporary Insurance Agreement, and 2.10 says the Minimum Initial Premium must be paid before delivery; the three do not line up exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence permitting payments 'at any time and in any amount' subject to the listed conditions; the qualification is express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four numbered conditions that follow, and 3.3's premium cap, are exactly the promised limits; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence survives only as a fragment ('The total of your premium payments during ... Premium shown in Section I'), so the obligation it imposes cannot be read off the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.2(2) and 2.9 state the same two-year minimum more fully, so the gap is fillable from elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed cumulative test (one-twelfth of annual Planned Periodic Premium times elapsed months, measured each of the first twenty-four months); arithmetically specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the no-lapse guarantee in 5.10 almost word for word, save that 5.10 subtracts withdrawals and indebtedness; the two tests are related but not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A floor on remittances plus a unilateral right to change it 'at any time' with notice; broad but expressly reserved and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.9's reference to the Minimum Premium Remittance shown in Section 1; nothing contradicts the change right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause reserves discretionary limits on additional premiums and then says 'This will happen only if' payment would increase the difference between death benefit and Policy Account Value — a condition whose grammar leaves it unclear which of the reserved powers it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 3.3's tax-driven premium cap, which allows refusal of premium on a different ground; the two limits coexist but their interaction is unexplained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tax-qualification cap with an express remedy (refuse or return excess premium); the standard is external law rather than an ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside 3.2(4) and 4.2's power to modify death benefits for tax compliance, all pointing the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reinstatement window ('within five years after the expiration of the Grace Period and prior to the surrender of the Policy') is scrambled in the text and the opening condition is displaced to the end, obscuring the trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.10(2) says the Policy 'will terminate without value' if premium is not paid, which sits awkwardly with a five-year right to revive the same policy and with 3.4(4)'s use of pre-lapse values.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only 'Receipt of evidence of insurability of the [Insured]' survives, and 'evidence of insurability' is left to the insurer's satisfaction elsewhere without a stated standard here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2 and 6.3 use the fuller phrase 'satisfactory to us', so the shortened condition here is read against those; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The requirement — premium sufficient for the next two Monthly Insurance Charges — is quantitatively definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'Section 5.2' for the Monthly Insurance Charge, but 5.2 is the Interest Rate provision and the charge is defined in 5.3; a mis-citation a court would have to correct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reinstated indebtedness if unpaid; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4 (indebtedness deducted from proceeds) and 3.4(4) (pre-lapse values carried over).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause fixes the values used on reinstatement as those in effect at lapse, which is definite, though it speaks of 'Surrender Charges'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 and 5.6/5.9 use 'Surrender Fee' and 'Percent of Surrender Fee' rather than 'Surrender Charges', an unmatched label that a court would need to equate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence stops at 'will be the Mont[hly Due Date]', so the effective date of reinstatement is not stated in the clause as reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Other effective-date rules (6.2, 6.3, 7.2) all use the Monthly Due Date following approval, which supplies the missing content by analogy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line bar on reinstatement after the Policy has been returned for its Surrender Value; truncated but its sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 5.8 (all insurance terminates on surrender) and the 3.4 opening words 'prior to the surrender of the Policy'; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause pays 'the Surrender Value to you if the Insured is living and this Policy is in force' without saying that a surrender request is required, an omission that could be read as an unconditional call on value.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.8 supplies the surrender mechanism and 5.9 the withdrawal mechanism, and 2.5 defines Proceeds to include surrender; read together the clause is workable but its unconditional phrasing is in tension with 5.8's request requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A spendthrift sentence qualified by 'to the extent permitted by law'; the qualification is standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere addresses creditor claims; 8.3 assignment rights are a different subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence stating that the death amount depends on Specified Amount and Coverage Option in effect; it is truncated but purely referential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Option A and Option B formulas that follow supply the content, and Section 1 shows Option A in force; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'greater of' formula with a premium add-back and a corridor percentage; the arithmetic is specified, though 'increased by any premiums received since the prior Monthly Due Date' sits oddly with the separate premium add-back later in 4.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The later 4.2 paragraph also adds 'premiums received after the date of death', raising a possible double count with limb 1 here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Option B's greater-of formula mirrors Option A and is arithmetically definite; the corrupted 'prior to our coinciding with' is a transcription slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.14's description of Option B and with 5.9's statement that Option B withdrawals reduce the death benefit; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence increases death benefits by 'any premiums received after the date of death', an odd and arguably erroneous rule, and decreases them by indebtedness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps limb 1 of Coverage Option A (premiums since the prior Monthly Due Date) and 9.4/5.10(3) (indebtedness and unpaid premium deducted from Proceeds), so the same adjustments appear in more than one place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurer may modify death benefits for tax compliance 'However, you have the right to refuse any modification' — the clause does not say what happens to the policy or its tax status if the owner refuses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against 3.3, under which the insurer will limit premiums precisely to preserve tax qualification, leaving the two compliance mechanisms unreconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest on death proceeds at a rate 'determined by us but never less than the rate required by the state in which the Insured resides' — discretionary but floored by an external standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.11 and 5.6 use the state 'in which this Policy is delivered' as the reference jurisdiction, while this clause uses the Insured's state of residence at death; a genuine mismatch of reference states.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The account-value formula 'A + B + C - D - E' is reproduced without its component definitions, so the central valuation mechanic cannot be applied from the clause itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to the Monthly Insurance Charge 'as described in Section 2' while the operative charge provision is 5.3, and the account value drives 4.2, 5.6, 5.7 and 5.10 throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical example is arithmetically wrong on its face — '6% less 2 points equals 6%' — a mechanical error in the very illustration of the loan-offset rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The actual Policy Loan Interest Rate lives in Section 1 and 9.3, so the error is contained, but it invites argument about the crediting rate on loaned account value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The monthly charge is defined as Cost of Insurance plus rider costs deducted on each Monthly Due Date; definite despite the scrambled word order.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 2.15 and 5.5, though 2.15 mis-cites Section 4.3 and 5.4 speaks of a 'Premium Due Date'; the substance nonetheless aligns.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause fixes COI as 'A x (B-C)' on 'any Premium Due Date' — a term the policy never defines — and leaves current rates to be 'determined by us based on our expectation of future experience', a classic open-ended discretionary standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Charges are made on the Monthly Due Date under 2.17 and 5.3, not a Premium Due Date, and the guaranteed table is said to be 'per $1,050' rather than the usual $1,000; both need reconciling with the rest of Section 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-limb adjustment for special risk classes survives only in pieces, with limbs (a) and (b) severed from their operations, so the rate adjustment cannot be computed from the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the 5.4 guaranteed-maximum table and Section 1's risk class ('STANDARD'), so it may have no application on these facts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line referral of rider costs to Section 1; nothing indeterminate in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.15, 2.16 and 5.3, all of which treat rider costs as separate from the Cost of Insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Cash Value formula gives components A, B and C but no operators, and 'C' — the difference between interest actually credited and guaranteed interest over the preceding twelve months — is an unexplained recapture item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cash Value feeds 5.7 Surrender Value, 5.9 withdrawals and 9.4's lapse trigger, so an unstated formula has consequences across Sections 5 and 9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Surrender Value is Cash Value less Policy Indebtedness — a two-line, arithmetically definite rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used as the lapse measure in 5.10 while 9.4 states the same test as Cash Value less indebtedness; the two are mathematically the same, so no real conflict.
